born: c. 1400-1405 (dates as commonly given; not verified in this session)
role_place: Constantinople, Ottoman period: first Ecumenical Patriarch after 1453 (1454-1456 per usual dating, not verified here) and a second term later.
why_relevant: Wrote the Christian creed-homily addressed to Mehmed II's Muslim scholars (PG 160, col. 333-352), the one major Orthodox text of this period presented to Muslims; he wrote little that names Muhammad in what I read.
fame: Known mainly as a scholastic theologian and as the patriarch who accepted the Ottoman order; the Confession to Mehmed II is his best-known work on Islam. A Cambridge article by Angeliki Ziaka (Studies in Church History) discusses him with George Amiroutzes on Islam; I saw only a search snippet of it, not the article.

born: c. 1400 (as in the Bonn/Bekker catalogue record; not verified)
role_place: Lesbos/Aegean and Constantinople; author of the Historia Byzantina (Turco-Byzantina), a narrative from 1341 to 1462.
why_relevant: Contemporary Greek historian who calls the Ottoman sultans antichrist-like and reports the religious oaths and claims of Bayezid and Mehmed II in theological terms, though his Islam content is scattered rather than doctrinal.
fame: Widely used historian of the fall of Constantinople; his use of the Muslim religious vocabulary is cited in general surveys (specific scholarly citations not checked in this session).
orthodox_status: historian / layman (Orthodox, Lesbian-Genoese world; no canonical status)

role_place: Protovestiarios and close adviser/envoy of Emperor Constantine XI; eyewitness of 1453; the Chronicon minus is the text attributed to him.
why_relevant: Eyewitness of the fall; his Chronicon maius contains the longest Greek polemic against Muhammad in the Bekker text I read, but that work is widely doubted as Sphrantzes' own (see limits).
fame: Known for the Chronicon (minus), a main source for 1401-1477; the Chronicon maius is the longer and disputed redaction. Scholarly disputes are reported in a Cambridge guide snippet (not opened).
orthodox_status: court official / layman (late monastic profession reported in tradition, not verified)
